title: staircase-kernel-todo-log-noor
body:
Late shift scratchpad — staircase experiment & kernel triage

Quick context:
- Running a small experiment with a dynamic batching heuristic I nicknamed 'staircase' (aggressive small-batch ramping then decay). Goal: reduce p99 for mixed short/long workloads without killing throughput.
- Not productioned, prototype in local-serving branch. Hit a few weird kernel-level IO/contention things overnight.

Today (2025-11-03) timeline / notes:
- 21:15 — pushed local change: staircase window=6, ramp_factor=1.5, decay=0.8.
- 21:27 — observed immediate drop in p95 but p99 climbed for seq>2048 requests.
- 21:33 — kernel logs: repeated WARN: kv-cache: eviction-stall (thread 7). Correlated with GC spikes in feeder thread.
- 22:02 — tried reducing ramp_factor->1.2, p99 improved marginally. But saw CPU steal on GPU host (noisy neighbor).
- 22:40 — reverted staircase in canary route; routed small percent back to baseline model. p99 returned to expected.

Metrics snapshot (local perf run, 5000 reqs mixed):
- baseline: p50=14ms, p95=88ms, p99=230ms, throughput=420r/s
- staircase (initial): p50=12ms, p95=70ms, p99=310ms, throughput=430r/s
- staircase (tuned ramp=1.2): p50=13ms, p95=75ms, p99=265ms, throughput=425r/s

Hypotheses / diagnostic leads:
1) kv-cache eviction-stall indicates we thrash the LRU list when ramping aggressively — maybe the staircase creates many short-lived prefixes that expand KV usage then drop.
2) feeder thread GC: we are allocating more ephemeral structures per request during ramp; need to check allocator churn (jemalloc arenas?).
3) Interaction with host-level noise — some of the p99 bump may be unrelated to our logic (seen CPU steal). Need clean repro on dedicated instance.

Quick repro steps (local):
- checkout: git checkout feat/staircase-local
- build: ./scripts/build-runtime --fast
- run: ./bin/serve-local --model gpt-small --batch-policy=staircase --window=6 --ramp=1.5 --decay=0.8 --kv-size=8g
- load test: locust -f tests/locust/mixed-workload.py --headless -u 500 -r 50 -t 5m
- capture logs: tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/runtime.log | grep -E "kv-cache|eviction|WARN|ERROR" > /tmp/staircase-logs.txt

Minimal instrumentation to add before next run:
- increment a per-request counter for "staircase ramp events" and log every 1000th occurrence to avoid noise.
- emit kv-cache occupancy histogram (buckets by entries and bytes) every 30s.
- add jemalloc stats dump (if enabled) on eviction-stall events.

Things to try (short list):
- decrease window to 4, keep ramp=1.2 — see if it reduces churn.
- change staircase to preserve prefix identities for short sessions (avoid creating distinct per-request kv keys).
- run on a dedicated host (no other tenants) to rule out CPU steal.
- toggle jemalloc tunables (decay_ms) in a dedicated run.

Open TODOs (for me / handoff):
- [ ] Add KV occupancy hist and emit to metrics (PR: small change in cache.cc) — aim EOD.
- [ ] Instrument ramp event counter + sampling logs.
- [ ] Reproduce on dedicated staging instance and collect perf profile (perf, flamegraph).
- [ ] If repro: add short-term mitigation: cap staircase max-window or fall back to baseline when KV occupancy > 70%.
- [ ] Draft a short postmortem if p99 regressed in canary once we have root cause.

Handoff summary (what I did and what to look at):
- What I changed: staircase policy (window, ramp, decay), briefly canaried to 5% traffic.
- What I saw: p95 improved but p99 regressed under long sequences; eviction-stall WARNs in runtime.log.
- Immediate next step: add KV occupancy telemetry + run isolated repro.
- If you pick this up: prioritize repro on dedicated instance; if noisy neighbor suspected, spin a fresh VM in us-west2-c with same instance type.

Notes for whoever picks up (Aisha / Ethan):
- Aisha: can you take the dedicated repro? match the host type we use in dedicated tests (g5.xlarge equiv). Collect `perf record` and `scalene` trace.
- Ethan: please add the kv-cache histogram + ramp counter logs. Keep sampling low frequency to avoid metric overload.

Random fringe thoughts (brain dump):
- 'Staircase' might be better applied only when short/short-only traffic detected — i.e., route based on expected seq length distribution per-user.
- Consider a shadow-run mode: run staircase decision but don't actually change batching; collect decision metrics to evaluate offline. Low-risk way to get distribution.

Questions I couldn't answer tonight:
- Is eviction-stall a symptom or root cause? (need profile)
- Why GC spikes correspond exactly to eviction-stall timestamps? (investigate allocation patterns)
- Are certain endpoints (chat vs. completion) disproportionately triggering it? (need per-route breakdown)

Small checklist before I sign off:
- [ ] push kv occupancy PR branch (WIP)
- [ ] add runbook note in confluence (link above)
- [ ] message #runtime-ops with brief summary + pointer to this file

Handoff tag: @aisha @ethan — ping in morning if no repro by then.

-- Noor
